clue.text: Bound to deal with dull hair that lies flat in the boudoir?

definitions.text: that lies flat in the boudoir
definitions.note: a relative clause standing for 'something that lies flat', a noun

parts.note: to bound is to leap or spring
mat is a variant spelling of matt, meaning lacking shine
a tress is a lock of hair

explanation.surface: Someone is obliged to tackle their lacklustre hair before bed in a lady's boudoir.
explanation.walkthrough: Mind the spelling: dull is the single-T variant MAT here, so it joins TRESS without a doubled T.
explanation.definitionFit: A bed's sprung base layer is the soft object that lies horizontally in any bedroom, the boudoir being a lady's private chamber.

clue.text: Vandals tearing apart items in fast-food outlet

indicators.note: something torn apart is broken up, so the letters are pulled out of their order and rebuilt

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written; it doubles as fodder

explanation.surface: Hooligans wreck the fittings of a burger bar or chip shop.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tearing' looks like part of the indicator but its letters are fodder too; only 'apart' is left to signal the rearrangement, read with it.
explanation.definitionFit: Salt and vinegar are the condiments sitting on the counter of a chip shop or takeaway, for sprinkling over fries.

clue.text: True stories neglected — so it possibly may not be the agency

indicators.note: possibly signals one possible rearrangement of the remaining letters rather than their given order
neglected letters are left out, so the two short words that follow are dropped from the phrase

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written, to be removed
taken as written, to be removed

explanation.surface: A jibe that a press service ignoring true stories might not deserve the name.
explanation.walkthrough: Strike S, O, I and T from TRUE STORIES and rearrange the seven letters left.
explanation.definitionFit: Reuters is the famous international news agency supplying stories to papers and broadcasters.

clue.text: Not wanting say to be stifled, I had to discuss terms

indicators.note: something stifled is smothered and held inside, so these letters go within the word for not

parts.note: taken as written
e.g. means for example, as 'say' does
taken as written
to have a meal is to eat it, so had is ATE

explanation.surface: Reluctant to have their voice silenced, someone had to sit down and bargain.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Not wanting say' reads as being denied a voice, but 'wanting' is only a joint: the word not wants the abbreviation for say tucked inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: To negotiate is to bargain over and discuss the terms of a deal or agreement.

clue.text: Man hides disgusting body — a huge white flabby thing?

indicators.note: to hide something is to keep it inside, so the man's name wraps around the other letters

parts.note: Mick is a man's name

indicators.note: disgusting describes something in a revolting state, so the word after it is mangled into a new order

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A grisly crime story: a man conceals a revolting corpse.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Disgusting' looks like it describes the body, but it signals the letters of body are jumbled before going inside MICK.
explanation.definitionFit: Moby Dick is the great white sperm whale of Melville's novel, a massive pale creature padded with blubber.

clue.text: The short run made by one in flight?

indicators.note: short means cut off, so the last letter of the first word is lost

parts.note: taken as written
to rush is to run hastily

explanation.surface: A brief dash, as by a fugitive on the run.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Flight' suggests fleeing, which suits the run, but here it means flying.
explanation.definitionFit: A thrush is a songbird, and birds are creatures one sees flying through the air.

clue.text: Gun left buried in common

indicators.note: something buried in lies inside, so the letter goes within the next word

parts.note: rife means widespread or common
L is the standard abbreviation for left

explanation.surface: A firearm abandoned and buried on the village common.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Common' looks like a piece of land where a gun might be buried, but it is the adjective meaning widespread.
explanation.definitionFit: A rifle is a long-barrelled firearm, one particular kind of gun.

clue.text: In which one sees gritty performances from youngsters?

definitions.text: In which one sees gritty performances from youngsters?

parts.note: surface reading: a hard-hitting play put on by young actors

parts.words: In which one sees gritty performances from youngsters?
parts.note: setter's reading: the place where small children play in actual grit

explanation.walkthrough: Gritty usually means tough and realistic, as of drama; here it is literal, and the performances are toddlers playing.
explanation.definitionFit: A sandpit is a playground box of sand where young children dig and play.

clue.text: Heroine from clan of old with drama unfolding

indicators.note: unfolding opens things out of their present shape, so the letters are spread into a new order

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A heroine emerges from an old Highland clan as a dramatic story unfolds.
explanation.walkthrough: Flora MacDonald is the Scotswoman who helped Bonnie Prince Charlie escape after Culloden in 1746, so the clan surface fits.
explanation.definitionFit: She is celebrated in Scottish history and song as a Jacobite heroine for smuggling the prince to Skye.

clue.text: Pub with no parking, no lager — shambolic place for a drink!

indicators.note: shambolic means chaotic and disorganised, so the letters are thrown into a new order
with no parking means the abbreviation for parking is taken out of the word before

parts.note: taken as written
P is the road-sign abbreviation for parking
taken as written

explanation.surface: A grumble about a pub with no car park and no lager, a hopeless place to drink.
explanation.walkthrough: The 'no' of 'no lager' is fodder, not a second deletion. A lounge bar is the more comfortable room of a traditional British pub.
explanation.definitionFit: A lounge bar is a room in a pub where customers sit and drink, so it is a drinking place.

clue.text: Irrefutable findings from staff in a laboratory

indicators.note: findings from means things found inside the words that follow, run across their boundaries

parts.note: the end of staff, then in, a, and the start of laboratory

explanation.surface: Scientists in a lab produce results nobody can dispute.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Findings' suits a laboratory but here signals that letters are found inside the next words.
explanation.definitionFit: A final verdict or decision is conclusive and cannot be appealed or argued with.

clue.text: Expert in a small part of the company

parts.note: taken as written
dept is the short form of department, a section of a firm

explanation.surface: A specialist working in one small division of a firm.
explanation.definitionFit: Adept is an adjective and noun for someone highly skilled, a master of something.

clue.text: Girl's mood conveyed in paint

parts.note: Di is a girl's name, with the 's attached
a temper is a state of mind or mood

explanation.surface: A young woman expresses her feelings through painting.
explanation.definitionFit: Distemper is a cheap water-based paint mixed with glue, once used for walls and scenery.

clue.text: Ship seen in channel around spring

indicators.note: around means the channel word surrounds the word for spring

parts.note: a ditch is a channel dug for water
a spa is a mineral spring

explanation.surface: A vessel spotted in a waterway near a fountain or stream.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ship' looks like a noun for a vessel, which the channel supports, but it is the verb meaning send.
explanation.definitionFit: To ship goods is to send them off, which is what to dispatch them means.

clue.text: Stop army male becoming aggressive little fellow?

parts.note: to ban something is to stop it
TA is the Territorial Army, Britain's volunteer reserve
M is the standard abbreviation for male

explanation.surface: Halt a male soldier who is turning violent.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark marks the definition as playful: a bantam is a small chicken, the cock famously combative.
explanation.definitionFit: A bantam is a small breed of domestic fowl whose cocks are pugnacious; the word also describes a feisty small person.

clue.text: A lamp at home hangs above grand landing

parts.note: taken as written
a lamp is a light
someone at home is in
G is short for grand, a thousand pounds

explanation.surface: A lamp in a house hangs over a grand staircase landing.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'hangs above' means the first pieces come before G; 'landing' is not part of a staircase but the act of coming down to land.
explanation.definitionFit: Alighting is the act of coming down and settling, as a bird or aircraft does when landing.

clue.text: It's taken up as a challenge, but it''s punishing for runners

definitions.text: It's taken up as a challenge
definitions.meaning: first meaning: the glove thrown down and picked up to accept a duel
second meaning: the double line of attackers someone is made to run between

explanation.walkthrough: The two senses are separate words historically: the glove of a challenge, and the military punishment in 'run the gauntlet'.
explanation.definitionFit: To take up the gauntlet is to accept a challenge; running the gauntlet was a punishment of being beaten while passing between two rows.

clue.text: King's one overthrown in modern republic

indicators.note: something overthrown is turned upside down, which in a word means read from the end back

parts.note: King Lear of Shakespeare's tragedy, with the 's
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A king is deposed and a new republic takes his place.
explanation.walkthrough: 'King' is not the usual R but a particular king, Lear.
explanation.definitionFit: The State of Israel was founded in 1948, making it a relatively recent parliamentary republic.

clue.text: Debauched man eating boy's food

indicators.note: eating takes something inside, so the debauched man swallows the next word

parts.note: a roué is a dissolute, debauched man
a lad is a boy

explanation.surface: A sinister picture of a rake consuming a boy's meal.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's after boy reads as possessive but is a joining 'has'.
explanation.definitionFit: A roulade is a rolled dish, such as a slice of meat or sponge wrapped around a filling.

clue.text: Savage, being sorrowful, is twitching

parts.note: sad means sorrowful
taken as written
a tic is an involuntary twitch

explanation.surface: A wild animal, miserable and quivering.
explanation.definitionFit: Savage as an adjective means fiercely cruel, as is someone who enjoys inflicting pain.

clue.text: In tribute, Blair gives high-level support for sailors

indicators.note: in places the prime minister inside the word that follows

parts.note: a toast is a tribute drunk to someone
Tony Blair was Prime Minister, PM

explanation.surface: Paying tribute, the Prime Minister offers his backing to the Navy.
explanation.walkthrough: Blair was the sitting UK Prime Minister when this appeared in 2001.
explanation.definitionFit: A topmast is the mast section above the lower mast on a sailing ship, literally a support high up for sails and rigging.

clue.text: Theologian exposed in papers as cheat

indicators.note: exposed in means shown inside, so the theologian's letters sit within the word for papers

parts.note: a file is a collection of papers
DD is Doctor of Divinity, the theology degree

explanation.surface: A churchman's fraud is revealed in the newspapers.
explanation.definitionFit: To fiddle is to swindle or falsify, as in fiddling one's expenses.

clue.text: Glee about foreign character's attempt to imitate someone good?

indicators.note: about means the word for glee goes round the foreign character

parts.note: elation is great joy, glee
mu is a letter of the Greek alphabet

explanation.surface: A singer of glee songs takes on a foreign role and mimics a fine performer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Glee' suggests the choral part-song, but it means joy.
explanation.definitionFit: Emulation is the effort to equal or surpass someone admired by copying them.

clue.text: Like tree drained of colour?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: made of or resembling a particular tree

explanation.walkthrough: The first sense is rare: the adjective from the ash tree, as wooden is from wood.
explanation.definitionFit: Ashen means pertaining to the ash tree, and also pale grey like ashes, as a shocked face is.

clue.text: Thick-skinned type in Augustine's home

definitions.meaning: first meaning: the large African river animal
second meaning: the North African city where St Augustine was bishop

explanation.walkthrough: 'Thick-skinned' usually means insensitive, a person; here it is literal.
explanation.definitionFit: The hippopotamus has a famously thick hide, and St Augustine of Hippo took his title from that Roman city.

clue.text: Cause to feel embarrassed in a social event

parts.note: taken as written
a bash is an informal party

explanation.surface: Someone is made to feel awkward at a party.
explanation.definitionFit: To abash someone is to make them ashamed or disconcerted.

clue.text: A country boy about to embrace a spiritual leader

indicators.note: about means turned round, so the phrase before it is read from the end backwards
to embrace is to hold within, so the turned phrase takes the final letter inside

parts.note: taken as written
Mali is a country in West Africa
a lad is a boy
taken as written

explanation.surface: A rural lad is about to hug a religious figure.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Country boy' reads as one rustic, but it is two pieces, a nation and a boy; 'about to' is not 'going to', the words split.
explanation.definitionFit: The Dalai Lama is the head monk of Tibetan Buddhism, revered as its spiritual guide.

clue.text: Foremost of impressionists in Tate deserving somehow to be looked at again

indicators.note: somehow means in some way or other, so the letters are put together in an unspecified new order
foremost of picks out only the leading letter of the next word

parts.note: the opening letter
taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: The leading Impressionist paintings at Tate Britain deserve a second look.
explanation.walkthrough: The Tate is the London gallery group; here its name is just four letters for the mix.
explanation.definitionFit: To be reinvestigated is to be examined or inquired into once more, looked at a second time.
